findings.fault: This heading is set in turquoise italic with an underline, so it looks exactly like a link, but it does nothing when tapped. It also uses the link look, which the other headings ("Surf", "Good for") don't.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone will tap it expecting a page about Canggu's vibe and get no response. That makes them doubt which of the page's other underlined words really are links.

findings.where: The "Good for" tags: First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays, Meeting people, Yoga, Nightlife, Budget, Cafés, Couples, Solo travellers, Scooter riders, Sunsets
findings.fault: These static facts are drawn as filled, outlined pills, which is how filter chips and buttons look, but none of them can be acted on. Each pill also gets its own fill and a clashing border colour (purple, pink, red, yellow, teal). The colours suggest categories that don't exist, and several sit off the brand palette or close to the coral that is kept for the one action. The row is the busiest thing on the page.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker will try to tap "Solo travellers" or "Budget" to filter hostels and nothing happens. The founder would object to colours with no job in a brand where every colour has exactly one.

findings.where: Nav "Destinations" and "How we rank", the wordmark's home link, and the footer links Privacy, Terms, How we rank and Report content
findings.fault: Every one of these links goes back to this same page. "Destinations" goes to #destinations, but the page shows no destinations section. The visitor has no way to move to another place or read the ranking method, privacy notice or terms.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker checking how hostels will be ranked, or what happens to their data, finds nothing behind the link. This undercuts the brand's promise that its ranking method is published, on a page that has no other next step.

findings.where: The "coming soon" announcement block above the footer
findings.fault: The notice is set on a saturated red ground that is not in the palette. Red reads as an error or an alarm, but the notice is calm news. The rules file puts this announcement on the ink night ground.
findings.who_objects: A visitor will read the red box as "something is broken" or "this place is unsafe" before reading what it says. The founder would object to an off-palette colour, and to the night pattern being broken on the one block it names.

findings.fault: The heading promises a ranked list of hostels, but the page has no hostels: listings are not live. The page actually delivers a guide to whether Canggu suits you. The h1 is also in title case, against the sentence-case voice rule.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from search wanting the best hostels scrolls to the end, finds only a "coming soon" note and feels misled. Search engines also judge the page against a promise it doesn't keep.

findings.where: The whole page: the first screen, and the end of the page above the footer
findings.fault: The page has no primary action and no next step. Once the visitor has read about Canggu, they can't move on to another destination, keep track of the launch, or reach anything useful. The page stops dead at the notice.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop leaves with nothing to do here. The founder loses the visitor at the one moment they are interested.

findings.where: The "What to look for" section (top of desktop-02, phone)
findings.fault: Half of the brief's job is "what to look for in a hostel there", yet this section is one sentence under a small, uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow. It is the weakest heading on the page and doesn't match the other section headings ("Surf", "Good for"), so the most useful advice gets the least weight.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker comparing hostels skims past the one part that helps them choose. A designer would object to section headings that don't share one treatment.

findings.where: Body text in the intro, the Surf, Vibe and What to look for sections, and the announcement block, worst in the announcement on phone
findings.fault: The text is fully justified, which opens wide, uneven gaps between words ("MantaHostels   is   launching   across" on phone, "Lively  and  social" on desktop).
findings.who_objects: A reader on a phone, often mid-transit, stumbles over the gaps, and the page looks less finished than the brand's "more craft" promise.

findings.where: The top of the page, and the desktop layout as a whole
findings.fault: There is no hero band, illustration or colour moment, though the rules make a destination page's top banner a loud, turquoise marketing zone. On desktop, the text column fills about a third of the width and leaves the right side empty. The chip rows and the announcement box run wider than the text column, so the edges don't line up and the box's text stops halfway across it.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object that the page reads sterile, which is the brand's named enemy, rather than beachy and energetic. A desktop visitor sees a lopsided page with no strong opening.

findings.where: The guide's claims: the Surf, Vibe and What to look for copy
findings.fault: No date or source tells the reader when this was checked or who wrote it. Statements like "one of the easiest places in Bali to learn" stand without anything behind them.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker knows Canggu changes fast and can't tell whether this advice is current. The brand stakes its value on being trusted.
